did_you_know.text: Did you know? In the seventh month, the Israelites gathered in Jerusalem "as one man," even though they were already living in their towns.

Did you know? The altar was set up on its foundations—that is, on its original site or designated place—and the people offered burnt offerings on it morning and evening despite their fear of the surrounding peoples.
Did you know? The returning exiles resumed observing the Feast of Booths and offered burnt offerings each day according to the prescribed number of sacrifices for that day.

Did you know? After the Feast of Booths, they continued offering the regular burnt offering, the offerings for the New Moons and appointed festivals, and the freewill offerings of those who volunteered.

Did you know? To build the Temple, they paid the craftsmen, as well as the Sidonians and Tyrians, to bring cedar logs from Lebanon to Joppa, in accordance with the authorization granted by Cyrus king of Persia.
Did you know? In the second year after their arrival in Jerusalem, the Levites aged twenty and older were appointed to supervise the work on the house of the Lord.

Did you know? The Levites worked together supervising the project; those mentioned among the overseers were Jeshua and his sons and brothers, Kadmiel and his sons, and the sons of Henadad and their fellow Levites.

Did you know? When the foundations of the Temple of the Lord were laid, the priests sounded trumpets and the Levites, the descendants of Asaph, played cymbals, following the arrangement established in the days of David king of Israel.
Did you know? As the foundations were being laid, the people sang praise and thanksgiving: "For he is good; his steadfast love toward Israel endures forever," and they shouted with a great shout.
Did you know? At that moment, two contrasting sounds were heard together: the older people who remembered the first Temple wept loudly, while many others shouted for joy.
